description: Ask whether anyone has already attested an artifact, BEFORE you install it or pay to scan it. Free and anonymous. Give a package identity like "chalk@5.6.1", an MCP server endpoint URL, or a sha256 content hash. Returns the signed verdict if one exists, which you can verify offline against https://lazaretto.dev/.well-known/jwks.json, plus freshness: whether the corpus has since contradicted it and whether it was attested under an older rules version. A miss is not a verdict, it only means nobody has scanned this yet. When nobody has attested an npm package identity, the answer falls back to a free identity check against published advisories: `answer: "identity_check"` with an `identity_check` object, and `found` still false, because an identity check is unsigned, looks at the identity rather than the code, and absence from the corpus is not a verdict. `identity_check.listed_as_malware: true` comes back as an error result, so a published malware version cannot be read as "nothing found"; `null` there means the corpus could not be consulted, which is unchecked and never clear.

subject.description: A package identity ("chalk@5.6.1"), an MCP server endpoint URL, or a sha256 content hash, optionally sha256: prefixed.

name: find_attestation

outputSchema.description: Check `contradicted` before acting: a stored clear verdict that the corpus now contradicts must not be trusted.

analysis_partial.description: Present and true when the attested verdict covered only part of the artifact. A clear verdict with this set is not a clean result.

answer.description: "identity_check" when nobody has attested the subject and a free advisory lookup answered instead.

attestation.description: Compact JWS you can verify offline; it carries the verdict, never the evidence.

contradicted.description: Non-null when this subject is NOW a known-bad match.

found.description: False means nobody has attested it, which is not a clean verdict.

identity_check.description: The fallback answer, never an attestation. `listed_as_malware` is true (published as malware, returned as an error), false (not in the corpus, which is not a verdict on the code), or null (the corpus could not be consulted: unchecked, never clear).

stale_rules.description: True when attested under an older rules version.
